findings.title: User mismatch check bypassed when Integration record missing
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, when `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `Integration.DoesNotExist`, the code returns `pipeline.next_step()` without performing the GitHub user mismatch validation (the very check this PR adds). This means if the webhook-created Integration has been deleted (or hasn't arrived yet due to timing), any GitHub user who knows a valid installation_id can complete the OAuth flow and proceed to build_integration, defeating the central security check of this PR. The `except Integration.DoesNotExist` branch should still perform the user validation, or alternatively should verify that `github_authenticated_user` was set by OAuthLoginView before allowing progress.

findings.title: Unguarded metadata['sender'] access can raise KeyError/TypeError
findings.body: The expression `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` will raise `KeyError` if `sender` is absent from metadata, or `TypeError` if `sender` is `None`/not a dict. Looking at `build_integration`, `sender` is only added when present in state (`if state.get("sender"):`), so older installations or webhook-created Integrations without sender info would crash with a 500 instead of producing the intended error page. The code should defensively check `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` before comparing.

findings.title: safe_urlopen not wrapped in try/except for OAuth token exchange
findings.body: `safe_urlopen(url=ghip.get_oauth_access_token_url(), data=data)` can raise on network errors or non-2xx GitHub responses, but only `safe_urlread`/`parse_qsl` are wrapped in try/except. A failure during the POST to GitHub's access_token endpoint will surface as an unhandled 500 rather than the intended "Invalid installation request." error page. The call should be inside the try block (or a separate try/except) so transient GitHub failures yield the same user-facing error as a missing/invalid token.

findings.title: Misleading comment about OrganizationIntegration
findings.body: The comment `# OrganizationIntegration does not exist, but Integration does exist.` precedes a `try: Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id, status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)` that does not consult OrganizationIntegration at all. The previous block already handled OrganizationIntegration via `installations_exist`; this block only checks for an active Integration. The comment should be reworded (e.g., "Active Integration already exists from a prior install; verify it belongs to the same GitHub user.") to match what the code actually does.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the 404 path
findings.body: The test stubs `/app/installations/{installation_id}` to return 404, then issues a callback with state `"ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05"` which does NOT match the pipeline signature `"9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3"`. The OAuthLoginView returns the generic error before ever reaching GitHubInstallation or build_integration, so the mocked 404 is never hit. With the correct state the test would also fail because no webhook was sent to create the Integration row, so GitHubInstallation's `Integration.DoesNotExist` branch returns `pipeline.next_step()` and build_integration is never called. The intended 404 behavior of `build_integration` (raising `IntegrationError("The GitHub installation could not be found.")`) is now untested.

findings.title: No dedicated test for OAuth state CSRF mismatch
findings.body: The only state-mismatch coverage is incidental inside `test_installation_not_found`, and even there it's combined with a missing-Integration path. There is no isolated test verifying that OAuthLoginView rejects a callback whose `state` query param differs from `pipeline.signature` and renders the failed-install template. A targeted regression test would protect this CSRF-style check from future refactors.

findings.title: No test for missing access_token from GitHub
findings.body: OAuthLoginView returns the generic error when `"access_token" not in payload` (covering GitHub returning an error response or empty body), but there is no test stubbing `https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token` to return e.g. `error=bad_verification_code` and asserting the pipeline terminates with the failed-install template. This branch is uncovered.

findings.title: No test for get_user_info returning no login
findings.body: OAuthLoginView also returns the generic error when `"login" not in authenticated_user_info`, but the only stub for `/user` returns a valid login. There is no test covering GitHub returning an error body from `/user` (e.g., missing scope or 401), which should likewise surface the failed-install page rather than a 500.
